investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod is stuck unscheduled. This is a cluster-level resource exhaustion condition localized to the kata peer-pods VM resource pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or the API surface. The eval failure is a direct reflection of this infrastructure constraint: because no pod ever reached a running state, the runner could not collect any of the four required evidence fields, causing the expected-output contract to report all evidence as missing.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — the scheduler message explicitly names resource exhaustion on the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable root cause, latencyMs=147890, endedAt=2026-07-16T03:30:35.580Z — a second independent pod submission hit the same capacity wall.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable root cause, latencyMs=150819, endedAt=2026-07-16T03:33:06.399Z — a third independent pod submission also failed to schedule.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — no evidence was written because the pod never started, so orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, and remoteState were never populated.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the probe aborting before createAgent could return.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=155899 — the check ran for ~156 s before timing out, which matches the scheduler's reported 150 s unscheduled window.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1884-1885: the runner calls requireOrgId then createAgent with machineType='remote'; if createAgent blocks waiting for a pod that never schedules, no evidence is written and the check fails.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:183: remote-agent-create is marked required=true with outageLatencyMs=360000; the observed latency of 155899 ms is within the warning threshold but the scheduling failure itself causes the hard fail.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing agents or leaked pods, leaving no capacity for new scheduling requests. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, meaning only 2 nodes are even eligible for remote-agent pods. If those 2 nodes lose capacity, the entire pool is unavailable. A misconfigured or overly restrictive affinity could shrink the eligible node set below what is needed.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: previously created agents that were not cleaned up may be consuming all available VM resource units, preventing new pods from scheduling.

Quaternary — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the 2 eligible nodes may be too small for the concurrent load, requiring additional nodes or increased per-node VM quotas.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes, resource exhaustion is not the cause and the scheduler message would need re-examination.

If a freshly submitted remote-agent pod schedules and reaches Running state immediately after the eval failure, the exhaustion was transient (e.g., a burst of concurrent requests) rather than a sustained capacity ceiling.

If the node affinity rules on the pod spec are found to be incorrect and actually exclude all 6 nodes (not just 4), the root cause would shift to a misconfiguration in the pod template rather than resource exhaustion.

If the eval runner's withCleanup function is found to have a bug that leaves pods in a broken state before the scheduling attempt, the failure could be an eval infrastructure defect rather than a cluster capacity issue.

If no kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is registered on any node (i.e., the extended resource was removed from the cluster), the cause would be a missing resource registration rather than exhaustion of an existing pool.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity across all nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, surfacing resource exhaustion as a distinct warning before the pod submission times out.

Add an eval that counts the number of currently running remote-agent pods and compares it against the total kata.peerpods.io/vm pool size, alerting when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%).
Add a zombie-pod detection eval that identifies remote-agent pods in Running or Pending state older than a configurable TTL and flags them for cleanup, preventing resource leaks from accumulating.
Add a node-eligibility eval that verifies at least N nodes match the remote-agent pod's node affinity selector, alerting when the eligible node count drops below a safe minimum.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message reporting zero available nodes: 2 nodes have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned an agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod submitted during this eval window was left in Unschedulable state for ~144–150 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet; this is an eval-level failure observed by the observability probe.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — the scheduler explicitly names kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion as the blocking condition.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=147890, status=fail — the eval ran for ~148 s before failing, consistent with the pod being stuck unscheduled for 144 s as stated in the message.
sibling.remote-agent-create: same scheduler error, pod stuck for 150 s, latencyMs=155899 — confirms the scheduling failure is not isolated to the state-polling probe.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: same scheduler error, pod stuck for 146 s, latencyMs=150819 — all three checks share the same root infrastructure constraint.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are absent — consistent with createAgent never completing because the pod never started.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1897-1905: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after requireOrgId — if the pod is never scheduled, this call blocks and eventually fails, preventing any evidence from being written.
source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:258-266: remote-agent-state contract requires orgId, agentId, readyState, state — none were produced because agent creation never succeeded.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the cluster has a fixed quota of peer-pod VM slots; concurrent workloads or a prior eval run consumed all available slots, leaving none for the probe pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 are already at VM capacity. If the affinity rules were broadened or more matching nodes were added, scheduling could succeed even without increasing per-node VM quota.

TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioning for concurrent eval load: if multiple eval runs or production workloads compete for the same kata.peerpods.io/vm slots simultaneously, transient exhaustion can occur without a persistent capacity deficit.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 affinity-matching nodes shows available capacity at the time of the failure, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and the cause would shift to a misconfigured resource request or quota limit on the pod spec itself.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure window succeeds without any cluster changes, it would suggest transient contention rather than a persistent capacity deficit.
If the pod scheduling error message changes on re-run (e.g., a different resource type is reported as insufficient), the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion diagnosis would need to be revised.

If the node affinity/selector rules on the pod spec were recently changed to restrict scheduling to fewer nodes, and those nodes were already at capacity for unrelated reasons, the affinity misconfiguration would be the primary cause rather than raw VM quota exhaustion.

If other non-remote-agent checks in the same eval run passed and also required Kubernetes pod scheduling, it would indicate the failure is specific to the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource type rather than a general cluster scheduling outage.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity before attempting remote-agent creation, and emits a warning or skip result with a capacity-exhausted message instead of waiting for a pod-stuck timeout.

Add a dedicated eval check for remote-agent pod scheduling health that verifies at least one kata.peerpods.io/vm slot is available on an affinity-matching node, decoupled from the full agent lifecycle checks.
Add a cleanup verification eval that confirms no orphaned remote-agent pods remain after each probe run, catching VM slot leaks before they exhaust cluster capacity.

Introduce a historical pass/fail trend eval for remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime so that repeated scheduling failures across runs are surfaced as a regression signal rather than appearing as isolated first-time failures (verifierContext.history.previousRunCount is currently 0).

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. The eval probe never reached the agent creation step, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state) is identical across all three sibling checks, confirming the failure is a shared infrastructure scheduling constraint, not an application-layer or eval-runner bug. Because the pod never scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1918) was never reached, leaving all required evidence fields empty and the contract validation failing with "Missing expected evidence: orgId, agentId, model, provider, message".

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error, latencyMs=147890, endedAt=2026-07-16T03:30:35.580Z — confirms the capacity problem persisted across the full eval window.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or prior eval runs consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new probe pods. This is the most strongly supported cause given the identical scheduler message across all three checks.

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: 4 of 6 nodes are permanently excluded by the pod's affinity/selector rules, artificially constraining the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes have limited VM capacity, any concurrent demand will exhaust it.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota across the 2 eligible nodes may be too small to handle simultaneous eval probe pods, especially if multiple eval runs overlap.

Lower confidence — a stuck or leaked VM from a prior eval run that was not cleaned up (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1916 implies cleanup is attempted, but a prior crash could leave a VM allocated), reducing available capacity for subsequent runs.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod is stuck unscheduled. This is a cluster-level resource exhaustion condition localized to the kata peer-pods VM resource pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or the API surface. The eval failure is a direct reflection of this infrastructure constraint: because no pod ever reached a running state, the runner could not collect any of the four required evidence fields, causing the expected-output contract to report all evidence as missing.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — the scheduler message explicitly names resource exhaustion on the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable root cause, latencyMs=147890, endedAt=2026-07-16T03:30:35.580Z — a second independent pod submission hit the same capacity wall.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable root cause, latencyMs=150819, endedAt=2026-07-16T03:33:06.399Z — a third independent pod submission also failed to schedule.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — no evidence was written because the pod never started, so orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, and remoteState were never populated.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the probe aborting before createAgent could return.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=155899 — the check ran for ~156 s before timing out, which matches the scheduler's reported 150 s unscheduled window.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1884-1885: the runner calls requireOrgId then createAgent with machineType='remote'; if createAgent blocks waiting for a pod that never schedules, no evidence is written and the check fails.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:183: remote-agent-create is marked required=true with outageLatencyMs=360000; the observed latency of 155899 ms is within the warning threshold but the scheduling failure itself causes the hard fail.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing agents or leaked pods, leaving no capacity for new scheduling requests. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, meaning only 2 nodes are even eligible for remote-agent pods. If those 2 nodes lose capacity, the entire pool is unavailable. A misconfigured or overly restrictive affinity could shrink the eligible node set below what is needed.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: previously created agents that were not cleaned up may be consuming all available VM resource units, preventing new pods from scheduling.

Quaternary — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the 2 eligible nodes may be too small for the concurrent load, requiring additional nodes or increased per-node VM quotas.

followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity across all nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, surfacing resource exhaustion as a distinct warning before the pod submission times out.

Add a zombie-pod detection eval that identifies remote-agent pods in Running or Pending state older than a configurable TTL and flags them for cleanup, preventing resource leaks from accumulating.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed ample remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the scheduling exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a different cause (e.g., a node affinity misconfiguration that newly excluded those nodes) would need to be investigated.

If the pod's node affinity/selector was recently changed to exclude nodes that previously had VM capacity, and the 2 remaining eligible nodes never had sufficient capacity, the root cause would shift to a configuration change rather than runtime exhaustion.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeded without any cluster changes, it would suggest a transient capacity spike (e.g., a concurrent workload that released VMs) rather than a persistent exhaustion condition.

If the remote-agent-create sibling check had passed while remote-agent-runtime failed, it would suggest the failure is isolated to the runtime probe rather than a shared scheduling constraint — but all three siblings failed, which supports the shared infrastructure cause.
If no kata.peerpods.io/vm resource is defined or allocatable on any node, the cause would be a missing resource registration rather than exhaustion.
